# Statistics

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## Array extensions where Element: Numeric

- `func sum() -> Element` — Returns the sum of all elements in the array. Returns: The sum of all elements, or zero for an empty array
- `func product() -> Element` — Returns the product of all elements in the array. Returns: The product of all elements
- `func cumulativeSum() -> [Element]` — Returns the running total at each position in the array. Returns: Array of running totals with the same length as the input
- `func cumulativeProduct() -> [Element]` — Returns the running product at each position in the array. Returns: Array of running products with the same length as the input

## Array extensions where Element: Comparable, Element: Numeric

- `func argMin() -> Int?` — Returns the index of the smallest element in the array. Returns: The index of the minimum element, or nil if the array is empty
- `func argMax() -> Int?` — Returns the index of the largest element in the array. Returns: The index of the maximum element, or nil if the array is empty

## Array extensions where Element: FloatingPoint

- `func mean() -> Element?` — Returns the arithmetic mean (average) of all elements in the array. Returns: The arithmetic mean, or nil if the array is empty
- `func median() -> Element?` — Returns the median (middle value) of the array. Returns: The median value, or nil if the array is empty
- `func variance(ddof: Int = 1) -> Element?` — Returns the variance of all elements in the array. Returns: The variance, or nil if the array has fewer elements than `ddof + 1`
- `func standardDeviation(ddof: Int = 1) -> Element?` — Returns the standard deviation of all elements in the array. Returns: The standard deviation, or nil if the array has fewer elements than `ddof + 1` *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func standardError(ddof: Int = 1) -> Element?` — Returns the standard error of the mean for the elements in the array. Returns: The standard error, or nil if the array has fewer elements than `ddof + 1` *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func zScore(of value: Element, ddof: Int = 1) -> Element?` — Standardizes a single value against this array's mean and standard deviation, returning how many standard deviations the value sits from the mean: `(value - mean) / standardDeviation`. Returns: The z-score of `value`, or nil if the array is empty, has fewer elements than `ddof + 1`, or has zero standard deviation (no spread to measure against). *(since 1.5.0)*
- `func skewness(bias: Bool = true) -> Element?` — Returns the sample skewness of the array — a single number describing how lopsided the distribution is. Returns: The skewness, or nil if the array has fewer than 3 elements, the standard deviation is zero, or any element is not finite. *(since 1.2.5)*
- `func kurtosis(bias: Bool = true) -> Element?` — Returns the sample excess kurtosis of the array — a single number describing how heavy the tails of the distribution are relative to a normal. Returns: The excess kurtosis (normal distribution has value 0), or nil if the array has fewer than 4 elements, the standard deviation is zero, or any element is not finite. *(since 1.2.5)*
- `func outlierMask(threshold: Element = Element(2), mean: Element? = nil, standardDeviation: Element? = nil) -> [Bool]` — Detects outliers using the z-score method and returns a boolean mask. Returns: Boolean mask where `true` indicates the element at that index is an outlier *(since 1.2.0)*

## Array extensions where Element == Double

- `func empiricalRule() -> EmpiricalRule?` — Returns the observed and expected fractions of values within one, two, and three sample standard deviations of the mean — the 68-95-99.7 rule applied to your data. Returns: An `EmpiricalRule` value containing observed and expected fractions, or nil if the array has fewer than two elements, the standard deviation is zero, or any element is not finite. *(since 1.2.5)*
- `func percentileCI(level: Double = 0.95) -> (lower: Double, upper: Double)?` — Returns the percentile-based confidence interval at the given coverage level. Returns: A `(lower, upper)` tuple of percentile bounds, or `nil` if the array is empty or `level` is outside `(0, 1)`. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func summary() -> ColumnSummary?` — Returns a typed snapshot of descriptive statistics: count, mean, std, min, quartiles, max, and iqr. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func skewnessReport() -> SkewnessReport?` — Returns a two-measure skewness diagnostic: the outlier-sensitive moment coefficient, the outlier-resistant Bowley coefficient, and whether the two agree. Returns: A `SkewnessReport`, or nil if either underlying measure is undefined — fewer than three values or zero spread (moment), or zero interquartile range (Bowley). *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func probability(of value: Double) -> Double` — Returns the relative frequency of `value` in the array. Returns: The fraction of elements equal to `value`, in the range `[0, 1]`. Returns `0.0` for an empty array. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func frequencyDistribution() -> [Double : Double]` — Returns a dictionary mapping each unique value to its relative frequency. Returns: A dictionary mapping each unique value to its relative frequency. Returns an empty dictionary for an empty array. *(since 1.1.0)*

## Array extensions where Element == [Double]

- `func meanVector() -> [Double]?` — Computes the element-wise mean across multiple vectors, producing a single vector where each dimension is the average of the corresponding dimensions across all inputs. Returns: A vector containing the mean of each dimension, or nil if the array is empty or vectors have inconsistent dimensions

## Array extensions where Element == [Float]

- `func meanVector() -> [Float]?` — Computes the element-wise mean across multiple vectors, producing a single vector where each dimension is the average of the corresponding dimensions across all inputs. Returns: A vector containing the mean of each dimension, or nil if the array is empty or vectors have inconsistent dimensions

## Array extensions where Element: Hashable

- `func mode() -> [Element]` — Returns the most frequently occurring value(s) in the array. Returns: An array of all values tied for highest frequency. Empty if input is empty. *(since 1.2.0)*

## Quartiles

`struct Quartiles<T> where T : BinaryFloatingPoint, T : Sendable` — The five-number summary plus the interquartile range for a sorted dataset. *(since 1.2.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let min: T` — The smallest value in the dataset. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let q1: T` — The 25th percentile — the value below which a quarter of the data falls. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let median: T` — The 50th percentile — the median. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let q3: T` — The 75th percentile — the value below which three quarters of the data falls. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let max: T` — The largest value in the dataset. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let iqr: T` — The interquartile range, defined as `q3 - q1`. Captures the spread of the middle 50% of the data. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `init(min: T, q1: T, median: T, q3: T, max: T, iqr: T)` *(since 1.2.0)*

## ColumnSummary

`struct ColumnSummary` — A frozen snapshot of descriptive statistics for a single numerical column. *(since 1.2.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let count: Int` — The number of values in the source column. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let mean: Double` — The arithmetic mean. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let std: Double` — The sample standard deviation (`ddof: 1`). *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let min: Double` — The smallest value. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let q1: Double` — The 25th percentile. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let median: Double` — The 50th percentile (median). *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let q3: Double` — The 75th percentile. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let max: Double` — The largest value. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `let iqr: Double` — The interquartile range, `q3 - q1`. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `init(count: Int, mean: Double, std: Double, min: Double, q1: Double, median: Double, q3: Double, max: Double, iqr: Double)` *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func markdownTable() -> String` — Renders the summary as a two-column Markdown table suitable for pasting into a deliverable. *(since 1.2.0)*
- `func csvRows() -> String` — Renders the summary as CSV with one row per statistic. *(since 1.2.0)*

## SkewnessReport

`struct SkewnessReport` — A two-measure skewness diagnostic: the moment coefficient, the robust Bowley coefficient, and whether the two agree. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let count: Int` — The number of elements summarized. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let moment: Double` — The adjusted Fisher-Pearson moment coefficient (sample convention). Unbounded; sensitive to outliers. Positive means a long tail toward high values, negative toward low values. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let bowley: Double` — The Bowley quartile coefficient `(Q3 - 2·Q2 + Q1) / (Q3 - Q1)`. Bounded to `[-1, 1]`; resistant to outliers because it uses only the quartiles. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `let agreement: SkewnessAgreement` — Whether the outlier-sensitive moment measure and the outlier-resistant Bowley measure agree, conflict by magnitude, or conflict in direction. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `init(count: Int, moment: Double, bowley: Double, agreement: SkewnessAgreement)` *(since 1.3.0)*

## Array extensions where Element: BinaryFloatingPoint

- `func bowleySkewness() -> Element?` — Returns the Bowley quartile coefficient of skewness — a robust measure built only from the quartiles, so a few extreme values cannot distort it. Returns: The Bowley coefficient, or nil if the array is empty, any element is not finite, or the interquartile range is zero (a constant or heavily-tied middle 50%, where the measure is undefined). *(since 1.3.0)*

## SkewnessAgreement

`enum SkewnessAgreement` — How an outlier-sensitive and an outlier-resistant skewness measure relate. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Hashable.

- `case agree` — Both measures land in their symmetric band, or both lean the same direction. The skew, whatever its size, is corroborated by a measure that ignores outliers. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case mixed` — One measure reads as roughly symmetric while the other reads as decisively skewed. The decisive measure is not corroborated — a sign that extremes may be at work. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case direction` — The two measures lean in opposite directions. The strongest signal that the moment number is driven by a few extreme values rather than the underlying shape. *(since 1.3.0)*

## EmpiricalRule

`struct EmpiricalRule` — Observed and expected fractions for the empirical (68-95-99.7) rule. *(since 1.2.5)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let count: Int` — The number of elements summarized. *(since 1.2.5)*
- `let within1Sigma: Double` — The observed fraction of values within one standard deviation of the mean. *(since 1.2.5)*
- `let within2Sigma: Double` — The observed fraction of values within two standard deviations of the mean. *(since 1.2.5)*
- `let within3Sigma: Double` — The observed fraction of values within three standard deviations of the mean. *(since 1.2.5)*
- `var expected1Sigma: Double { get }` — The fraction expected within one standard deviation for a Gaussian distribution (0.6827). *(since 1.2.5)*
- `var expected2Sigma: Double { get }` — The fraction expected within two standard deviations for a Gaussian distribution (0.9545). *(since 1.2.5)*
- `var expected3Sigma: Double { get }` — The fraction expected within three standard deviations for a Gaussian distribution (0.9973). *(since 1.2.5)*
- `init(count: Int, within1Sigma: Double, within2Sigma: Double, within3Sigma: Double)` *(since 1.2.5)*

## Array extensions where Element: Comparable, Element: Hashable

- `func distinct() -> [Element]` — Returns the unique values in the array, sorted in ascending order. Returns: The unique elements in ascending order. Returns an empty array for an empty input. *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func distinctCounts() -> [(value: Element, count: Int)]` — Returns each unique value paired with the number of times it appears. Returns: An array of `(value, count)` tuples sorted in ascending order by value. Returns an empty array for an empty input. *(since 1.1.0)*
